This report provides city council with an update on the community safety program, including the status, implementation, and performance of coordinated community safety plans operating across Saskatoon.

The program is a city-led partnership based framework that brings together municipal departments, sastion fire department, sastion police service, service providers, private security and community partners to coordinate responses to community safety pressures.
Currently, coordinated community safety plans are in place for several locations, experience a heightened activity, including the Pacific Avenue temporary shelter location.
We have a new C drop in location. Pleasant Hill and Riversdale Encounment Response area, and a pilot project at the 3rd Avenue and 23rd Street intersection.

These plans establish a structured and consistent approach to interagency coordination, enabling partners to align roles, share information, and adapt responses in real time based on emerging conditions.
The plan remains flexible in order to respond to the specific needs in the area.
We are working with the SFD and SPS to gather instant data for all of the downtown and Riversdale bid areas.
This will help in identifying hotspots and how they move around the areas.
We will adjust our responses to address these hotspots where possible.
Operational experience demonstrates that the coordinated model is functioning as intended.
In particular, the specific Avenue temporary shelter has demonstrated the effectiveness of aligning safety resources with service delivery,
supporting more stable day-to-day operations, and helping to mitigate impacts on surrounding areas.
This planning includes support from private sector to fill private security to fill identified gaps in supports.
This approach has informed the development and refinement of safety plans at other location, and reinforces the value of proactive planning and sustained collaboration.
This report outlines current operating conditions, highlights program performance, and identifies emerging pressures associated with increasing demands for services in 2026.
As noted in the report, volume and intensity of activity being managed has increased significantly in 2026.
It also describes how the community safety program continues to support service delivery, while managing impacts on neighborhoods and the importance of ongoing coordination,
monitoring and resource alignment to respond to evolving conditions.
